passages.text: And Saul was there, giving approval to Stephen’s death. On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.
passages.sermon:
Saul was present.
Saul approved of Stephen’s death.
A great persecution began that day.
The persecution targeted the church in Jerusalem.
All the believers except the apostles scattered.
They scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria.
passages.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ διωγμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις πάντες δὲ διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων

passages.text: God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.
passages.sermon: God-fearing men took Stephen’s body.\r\nThey buried Stephen.\r\nThey mourned deeply for Stephen.
passages.original: συνεκόμισαν δὲ τὸν Στέφανον ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ ἐποίησαν κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ

passages.text: But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man who opposed the church.
He began to destroy the church.
He went from house to house.
He dragged off men.
He dragged off women.
He put these people in prison.
passages.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους εἰσπορευόμενος σύρων τε ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν

passages.text: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.
passages.sermon: Persecution scattered many believers.\r\nThese scattered believers traveled to different places.\r\nThey preached the word of God everywhere they went.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον

passages.text: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a follower of Jesus.
Philip traveled to a city in Samaria.
Philip spoke to the people in that city.
Philip told them about Christ.
passages.original: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Χριστόν

passages.text: The crowds gave their undivided attention to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a Christian preacher.
He went to a city in Samaria.
He spoke to the people there.
Large crowds listened to Philip.
They paid close attention to his words.
They also watched the signs Philip performed.
The people saw what Philip did.
They listened to his message together, with one mind.
passages.original: προσεῖχον δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει

passages.text: With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a Christian preacher.
\r\nHe went to a city in Samaria.
\r\nHe proclaimed Christ to the people there.
\r\nMany people in the city had unclean spirits.
\r\nThese unclean spirits possessed them.
\r\nThe unclean spirits came out of many people.
\r\nThey came out with loud cries.
\r\nMany people in the city were paralyzed.
\r\nMany people in the city could not walk.
\r\nPhilip healed many of the paralyzed.
\r\nPhilip healed many of the lame.
passages.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ τῶν ἐχόντων πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα βοῶντα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξήρχοντο πολλοὶ δὲ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν

passages.text: So there was great joy in that city.
passages.sermon: The people in that city felt great joy.\r\nMany people rejoiced together.\r\nThe whole city experienced much happiness.
passages.original: ἐγένετο δὲ πολλὴ χαρὰ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ

passages.text: Prior to that time, a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria. He claimed to be someone great, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, heeded his words and said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”
passages.sermon:
A man named Simon lived in that city.
Simon practiced sorcery.
Simon amazed the people of Samaria.
Simon said he was someone great.
All the people listened to Simon.
People of every social rank paid attention to him.
They said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”
passages.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ὀνόματι Σίμων προϋπῆρχεν ἐν τῇ πόλει μαγεύων καὶ ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν ᾧ προσεῖχον πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ καλουμένη Μεγάλη

passages.text: They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.
passages.sermon:
Simon was a man in the city of Samaria.
Simon practiced sorcery.
Simon amazed the people with his magic.
The people of Samaria paid close attention to Simon.
Simon had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.
passages.original: προσεῖχον δὲ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς

passages.text: But when they believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a preacher.
Philip preached the good news.
He preached about the kingdom of God.
He preached about the name of Jesus Christ.
The people listened to Philip.
The people believed Philip.
Men believed.
Women believed.
The people were baptized.
Both men and women were baptized.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες

passages.text: Even Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.
passages.sermon:
Simon was a man who practiced sorcery in Samaria.
Simon believed the message about Jesus Christ.
Simon was baptized.
Simon stayed close to Philip.
Simon watched Philip perform great signs and miracles.
Simon was amazed by these signs and miracles.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Σίμων καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ θεωρῶν τε σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας γινομένας ἐξίστατο

passages.text: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
passages.sermon:
The apostles lived in Jerusalem.
The apostles heard news about Samaria.
Samaria had received the word of God.
The apostles decided to act.
The apostles sent Peter and John to Samaria.
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀπόστολοι ὅτι δέδεκται ἡ Σαμάρεια τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτοὺς Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην

passages.text: On their arrival, they prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon: Peter and John arrived in Samaria.\r\nThey prayed for the people in Samaria.\r\nThey asked God to give the Holy Spirit to these people.
passages.original: οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον

passages.text: For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
passages.sermon: The Holy Spirit had not come upon any of them.\r\nThey had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
passages.original: οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπ’ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός μόνον δὲ βεβαπτισμένοι ὑπῆρχον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon: Peter and John were apostles of Jesus Christ.\r\nPeter and John laid their hands on the people.\r\nThe people received the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: τότε ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτούς καὶ ἐλάμβανον Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον

passages.text: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money.
passages.sermon:
Simon was a man who watched the apostles.
He saw the apostles lay their hands on people.
He saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the apostles’ hands.
Simon wanted this power.
Simon gave the apostles money.
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Σίμων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων δίδοται τὸ Πνεῦμα προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα

passages.text: “Give me this power as well,” he said, “so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”
passages.sermon:
Simon spoke to the apostles.
Simon wanted the same power they had.
Simon said, “Give me this power also.”
Simon wanted to lay his hands on people.
Simon wanted people to receive the Holy Spirit when he laid his hands on them.
passages.original: λέγων Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον

passages.text: But Peter replied, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter spoke to Simon.
Peter said, “May your silver perish with you.
You thought you could buy the gift of God with money.
You cannot buy God’s gift with money.”
passages.original: Πέτρος δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Τὸ ἀργύριόν σου σὺν σοὶ εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθαι

passages.text: You have no part or share in our ministry, because your heart is not right before God.
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Simon.
Peter said, “You have no part in this ministry.
You have no share in this work.
Your heart is not right before God.”
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου οὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ἔναντι τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Simon.
Peter saw that Simon’s heart was not right before God.
Peter said, “Turn away from this evil you have done.
Ask the Lord to forgive you.
Maybe God will forgive the thoughts and plans in your heart.”
passages.original: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας σου ταύτης καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ Κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σου

passages.text: For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Simon.
Peter saw Simon’s true condition.
Simon was poisoned by bitterness.
Simon was a captive to iniquity.
passages.original: εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄντα

passages.text: Then Simon answered, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.”
passages.sermon:
Simon was a man who had practiced sorcery in Samaria.
Simon heard Peter’s rebuke and warning.
Simon answered Peter and John.
Simon said, “Pray to the Lord for me.”
Simon wanted Peter and John to pray on his behalf.
Simon asked this so that nothing they had spoken would happen to him.
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Σίμων εἶπεν Δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν Κύριον ὅπως μηδὲν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε

passages.text: And after Peter and John had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John were apostles of Jesus Christ.
Peter and John testified about Jesus.
Peter and John spoke the word of the Lord.
Peter and John returned to Jerusalem.
Peter and John preached the gospel in many Samaritan villages.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου ὑπέστρεφον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν εὐηγγελίζοντο

passages.text: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
passages.sermon:
An angel from the Lord spoke to Philip.
The angel gave Philip a command.
The angel said, “Get up.”
The angel said, “Go south.”
The angel told Philip to travel on the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.
This road is in the desert.
passages.original: Ἄγγελος δὲ Κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος

passages.text: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship, and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
passages.sermon:
Philip obeyed the angel and began his journey.
He met a man from Ethiopia.
This man was a eunuch.
He served as a high official under Candace, the queen of the Ethiopians.
He managed all the queen’s treasury.
He had traveled to Jerusalem to worship God.
He was now returning home.
He sat in his chariot.
He was reading from the book of the prophet Isaiah.
passages.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης αὐτῆς ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ ἦν τε ὑποστρέφων καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν τὸν προφήτην Ἠσαΐαν

passages.text: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit spoke to Philip.
The Spirit gave Philip a command.
The Spirit said, “Go to that chariot.”
The Spirit said, “Stay close to it.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμα τῷ Φιλίππῳ Πρόσελθε καὶ κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ

passages.text: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a follower of Jesus.
Philip obeyed the Holy Spirit.
Philip ran to the chariot.
Philip heard the Ethiopian eunuch reading.
The Ethiopian eunuch was reading the prophet Isaiah.
Philip spoke to the Ethiopian eunuch.
Philip asked, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
passages.original: Προσδραμὼν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην καὶ εἶπεν Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις

passages.text: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
passages.sermon:
The man was an Ethiopian eunuch.
He was reading the prophet Isaiah.
Philip asked him if he understood what he was reading.
The eunuch answered Philip.
He said, “How can I understand unless someone guides me?”
He asked Philip to help him.
He invited Philip to come up and sit with him in the chariot.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην ἐὰν μή τις ὁδηγήσει με παρεκάλεσέν τε τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ

passages.text: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
passages.sermon:
The eunuch was reading a passage from Scripture.
This passage described a person.
He was led like a sheep to be killed.
He was silent, like a lamb before the person who shears it.
He did not open His mouth.
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus suffered humiliation.
People took away justice from Jesus.
No one can describe the descendants of Jesus.
People took the life of Jesus from the earth.
passages.original: Ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”
passages.sermon:
A eunuch was reading a passage from Scripture.
He did not understand it.
Philip was with him.
The eunuch spoke to Philip.
He asked Philip a question.
He said, “Please tell me something.”
He asked, “About whom does the prophet speak?”
He asked, “Is the prophet talking about himself?”
He also asked, “Or is the prophet talking about someone else?”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τῷ Φιλίππῳ εἶπεν Δέομαί σου περὶ τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει τοῦτο περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ ἑτέρου τινός

passages.text: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a follower of Jesus.
Philip spoke to the eunuch.
Philip started with this Scripture.
Philip explained the good news.
Philip told the eunuch about Jesus.
passages.original: Ἀνοίξας δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς ταύτης εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”
passages.sermon:
Philip was a Christian preacher.
The eunuch was an important official from Ethiopia.
Philip and the eunuch traveled together on the road.
They came to some water.
The eunuch saw the water.
The eunuch spoke to Philip.
The eunuch said, "Look, here is water."
The eunuch asked, "What can stop me from being baptized?"
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι

passages.text: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a Christian preacher.
The eunuch was an important official from Ethiopia.
The eunuch wanted to be baptized.
The eunuch gave orders to stop the chariot.
Philip and the eunuch both went down into the water.
Philip baptized the eunuch.
passages.original: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν

passages.text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a follower of Jesus.
The eunuch was an important official from Ethiopia.
Philip baptized the eunuch in water.
They both came up out of the water.
The Spirit of the Lord took Philip away.
The eunuch did not see Philip anymore.
The eunuch continued on his journey.
The eunuch was full of joy.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων

passages.text: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
passages.sermon:
Philip was a Christian preacher.
Philip appeared at Azotus.
He traveled through that region.
He preached the gospel in every town.
He continued this until he came to Caesarea.
passages.original: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν
